intro: You already use will, going to and the present continuous for the future. Now you stand at a moment in the future and describe it three ways: what you'll be doing then (This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali), what you'll have done by then (By 2030 I'll have finished my degree), and how long you'll have been doing it (By June I'll have been working here for five years). Warm-up: what will you be doing at 9 tomorrow morning?
teachingNotes: Recap, don't re-teach: the learner has done b1-future-forms (will, going to, present continuous for arrangements, might/may, and the present after when/after/before/as soon as/until) and the present perfect simple and continuous (have + past participle, have been + -ing, for/since). Build the new forms on those: will be + -ing = the present continuous moved to a future moment; will have + past participle = the present perfect moved to a future moment; will have been + -ing = the present perfect continuous moved to a future moment. Explain 'past participle' as the third form they know from the present perfect (finished, sent, left, written, paid).

Future continuous (will be + -ing): an action in progress at a future moment, started before it and going on after it. Clues: this time tomorrow, this time next week, at 8 tonight, at 10 on Monday, from 9 to 12. Common error *'This time tomorrow I will fly to Bali' → 'This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali' (Indonesian 'Besok jam segini saya sedang terbang' has sedang, which learners drop). Contrast: At 8 I'll call you (starts at 8) vs At 8 I'll be driving (in the middle). be never changes after will (not *'she will is working'). Polite questions (Will you be using the car tonight? = asking about plans before a request) are a note only: don't test them. State verbs (know, want, like, believe, need, own) don't take -ing: *'you'll be knowing' → 'you'll know'.

Future perfect (will have + past participle): finished before a future moment. Key word by = paling lambat / sebelum atau tepat pada (by Friday, by 2030, by then, by the end of the year); with a verb, by the time + PRESENT simple (By the time you get here, the film will have started). by ≠ until: until = sampai, the action continues the whole time (I'll be at the office until 6). Indonesian trap: 'Tahun 2030 saya sudah lulus' → *'I already finish' or *'I have finished by 2030' (the present perfect can't go with a future time). have never changes (not *'she'll has left'); in speech have is weak ('I'll-ev left'), never written 'I'll of'. Common error *'By 2030 I will finish my degree': as a plan or promise, 'I'll finish the report by Friday' is acceptable English, so don't mark will + by wrong in a learner's free sentence; the future perfect is needed when you describe the situation at that moment, especially with by the time or already (By the time you wake up, I'll already have left; not 'I'll leave'). Only test those clear cases.

Future perfect continuous (will have been + -ing): a duration up to a future moment, usually with for + a period and a point (by June, next year, when the bus comes). Same form for every subject. Indonesian 'Juni nanti sudah lima tahun saya kerja di sini' → not *'In June I work here five years'. B2 tendency, not a hard rule: with live, work, study, teach, the future perfect simple is also correct (By June I'll have worked here for five years): accept it in open answers unless the task asks for the continuous. With state verbs (know, be, have for owning) only the simple works: By May I'll have known Sari for ten years.

Time clauses still take no will, not even will have or will be: after when, after, before, as soon as, until and by the time, use the present simple or the present perfect (to stress 'finished'). Common error *'Call me when you will have finished' → 'Call me when you have finished' (or 'when you finish'). Indonesian 'Kabari saya kalau sudah selesai' has sudah, which pushes learners to *'when you will have finished'. A question is different: 'When will you have finished?' is correct.

Limits: don't teach the future in the past (was going to, would), passive future forms (will have been done), shall, the third conditional, wish or past modals. Spelling of -ing (lie → lying, run → running) and irregular participles (leave → left, pay → paid) may come up: correct them gently. Use adult B2 contexts: deadlines, contracts, flights, startups, KRL and TransJakarta, careers, study abroad, rupiah.

keyPoints.title: will be + -ing: in the middle of it at a future moment
keyPoints.explanation: Use will be + -ing (the future continuous) for an action in progress at a moment in the future: it starts before that moment and goes on after it. Clues: this time tomorrow, at 8 tonight, at 10 on Monday. Simple will is different: At 8 I'll call you = the call starts at 8; At 8 I'll be driving = I'm in the middle of driving. Indonesian 'sedang' + a future time → will be + -ing, not 'I will fly'.

examples.en: This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.
examples.id: Besok jam segini saya sedang terbang ke Bali.

examples.en: Don't call me at 10. I'll be meeting a client.
examples.id: Jangan telepon saya jam 10. Saya sedang bertemu klien.

examples.en: I won't be working on Friday. I've taken a day off.
examples.id: Hari Jumat saya tidak bekerja. Saya sudah ambil cuti.

id.title: will be + -ing: sedang berlangsung pada saat tertentu di masa depan
id.explanation: Pakai will be + -ing (future continuous) untuk kegiatan yang sedang berlangsung pada saat tertentu di masa depan: kegiatannya mulai sebelum saat itu dan masih berjalan sesudahnya. Petunjuknya: this time tomorrow (besok jam segini), at 8 tonight, at 10 on Monday. will biasa berbeda: At 8 I'll call you = teleponnya mulai jam 8; At 8 I'll be driving = jam 8 saya sedang di tengah perjalanan menyetir. 'sedang' + waktu masa depan → will be + -ing, bukan 'I will fly'.

keyPoints.title: will have + past participle: done by a future moment
keyPoints.explanation: Use will have + past participle (the future perfect) for something finished before a moment in the future. The past participle is the third form from the present perfect (finished, sent, left). The key word is by = no later than (by Friday, by 2030, by then); with a verb, by the time + present simple. Indonesian 'sudah' + a future time → will have + past participle, not 'I already finish'. by is a deadline; until means the action continues the whole time.

examples.en: By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.
examples.id: Paling lambat tahun 2030 kuliah saya sudah selesai.

examples.en: By the time we get there, the film will have started.
examples.id: Saat kita sampai nanti, filmnya sudah mulai.

examples.en: She won't have finished her shift by 9.

id.title: will have + past participle: sudah selesai pada saat tertentu di masa depan
id.explanation: Pakai will have + past participle (future perfect) untuk hal yang sudah selesai sebelum saat tertentu di masa depan. Past participle adalah bentuk ketiga yang kamu kenal dari present perfect (finished, sent, left). Kata kuncinya by = paling lambat (by Friday, by 2030, by then); dengan kata kerja, by the time + present simple. 'sudah' + waktu masa depan → will have + past participle, bukan 'I already finish'. by itu tenggat; until berarti kegiatannya berlangsung terus sampai saat itu.

keyPoints.title: will have been + -ing: how long, up to a future moment
keyPoints.explanation: Use will have been + -ing (the future perfect continuous) for a duration up to a moment in the future: for + a period, plus the moment (by June, next year, when …). It's the present perfect continuous moved into the future. With live, work, study, will have worked is also fine; with state verbs (know, be) use only the simple: I'll have known her for ten years.

examples.en: By June I'll have been working here for five years.
examples.id: Juni nanti, sudah lima tahun saya bekerja di sini.

examples.en: Next month Rina will have been learning English for three years.
examples.id: Bulan depan sudah tiga tahun Rina belajar bahasa Inggris.

examples.en: By 9 pm the team will have been working on the app for twelve hours.
examples.id: Jam 9 malam nanti, tim itu sudah dua belas jam mengerjakan aplikasinya.

id.title: will have been + -ing: sudah berapa lama, sampai saat tertentu di masa depan
id.explanation: Pakai will have been + -ing (future perfect continuous) untuk lamanya kegiatan sampai saat tertentu di masa depan: for + lamanya, ditambah saatnya (by June, next year, when …). Ini present perfect continuous yang dipindah ke masa depan. Dengan live, work, study, will have worked juga benar; dengan kata kerja keadaan (know, be) pakai bentuk simple saja: I'll have known her for ten years.

assessment.prompt: Find the mistake and write the correct sentence: This time next week I will lie on a beach in Lombok.
acceptableAnswers: this time next week i'll be lying on a beach in lombok
this time next week i will be lying on a beach in lombok
this time next week ill be lying on a beach in lombok
i'll be lying on a beach in lombok this time next week
i will be lying on a beach in lombok this time next week
assessment.rubric: Correct: This time next week I'll be lying on a beach in Lombok (will be + -ing: in the middle of it at that moment; lie → lying). 'will be lieing' = 80 (spelling). 'will be laying' = 70 (lay/lie mix-up, but the form is right). 'will be lie' = 40. 'I'm lying' = 30. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with will and the verb in brackets. Budi's driving test (ujian SIM) is from 2 to 3 tomorrow afternoon. He tells his mum: 'Don't call me at 2:30. I ___ (take) my driving test then.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: 'll be taking / will be taking (at 2:30 the test is in progress). 'will take' = 40 (sounds like it starts at 2:30). 'am taking' = 40 (the task asks for will). 'will be take' = 50. 'will have taken' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the verb in brackets. Budi is still at his office on Jalan Sudirman at 11:45 pm. He thinks: 'By the time I get to Manggarai station, the last KRL ___ (leave). I'll have to take an ojek.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: will have left (done before he arrives: will have + past participle; leave → left). 'will have leave' or 'will have leaved' = 50. 'will leave' = 30. 'has left' or 'left' = 20. 'will be leaving' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the verb in brackets. Sari is making the last payment for her motorbike in March. She says: 'By April, I ___ (pay) for it completely. No more instalments!'
assessment.rubric: Correct: 'll have paid / will have paid (done before April; pay → paid). 'will have payed' = 70 (spelling). 'will pay' = 40. 'have paid' or 'already pay' = 30 (no future).

assessment.prompt: Find the mistake and write the correct sentence: Text me when you will have arrived at the hotel.
acceptableAnswers: text me when you have arrived at the hotel
text me when you've arrived at the hotel
text me when youve arrived at the hotel
text me when you arrive at the hotel
text me when you get to the hotel
assessment.rubric: Correct: Text me when you've arrived / when you have arrived / when you arrive at the hotel (no will after when, even for the future). 'when you will arrive' = 30. 'when you arrived' = 30. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the future perfect continuous of the verb in brackets. Pak Hasan opened his warung in Surabaya in December 2016. He says: 'By this December, I ___ (run) it for ten years!'
assessment.rubric: Correct: will have been running (how long, up to a future moment; run → running, double n). 'will have been runing' = 80 (spelling). 'will have run' = 70 (correct future perfect simple, but the task asks for the continuous). 'have been running' = 40 (true now, but the sentence is about December). 'will be running' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the future perfect continuous of wait. Rina started waiting for the TransJakarta bus at 7:00. It's 7:40 now, and the app says the bus will come at 8:00. Rina: 'When the bus comes, I ___ for an hour!'
assessment.rubric: Correct: will have been waiting (how long, from 7:00 up to 8:00 when the bus comes). 'will have waited' = 70 (correct, but the task asks for the continuous). 'have been waiting' = 40. 'will be waiting' = 30. 'will wait' = 10.

material.title: will be + -ing: in the middle of it

blocks.text:
**will be + -ing** (the **future continuous**) describes an action that is **in progress** at a moment in the future. It started before that moment and goes on after it. Typical clues: **this time tomorrow**, **this time next week**, **at 8 tonight**, **at 10 on Monday**.
- Positive: *I'll be flying*, *She'll be working*
- Negative: *I won't be working*
- Question: *Will you be working?*

**be** never changes after will: *She will be working*, not 'She will is working'.

Compare it with simple **will**: *At 8 I'll call you* = the call **starts** at 8. *At 8 I'll be driving* = at 8 I'm **in the middle** of driving.

id.text:
**will be + -ing** (**future continuous**) menggambarkan kegiatan yang **sedang berlangsung** pada saat tertentu di masa depan. Kegiatannya mulai sebelum saat itu dan masih berjalan sesudahnya. Petunjuk yang biasa muncul: **this time tomorrow** (besok jam segini), **this time next week** (minggu depan jam segini), **at 8 tonight**, **at 10 on Monday**.
- Positif: *I'll be flying*, *She'll be working*
- Negatif: *I won't be working*
- Pertanyaan: *Will you be working?*

**be** tidak pernah berubah setelah will: *She will be working*, bukan 'She will is working'.

Bandingkan dengan **will** biasa: *At 8 I'll call you* = teleponnya **mulai** jam 8. *At 8 I'll be driving* = jam 8 saya **sedang** menyetir.

rows.en: This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.
rows.id: Besok jam segini saya sedang terbang ke Bali.
rows.note: in the air at that moment

rows.en: Don't call me at 10. I'll be meeting a client.
rows.id: Jangan telepon saya jam 10. Saya sedang bertemu klien.
rows.note: the meeting is going on at 10

rows.en: At 8 tonight we'll be having dinner at Bu Ani's.
rows.id: Nanti malam jam 8 kami sedang makan malam di rumah Bu Ani.
rows.note: in the middle of dinner at 8

id.note: jam 8 sedang di tengah makan malam

rows.en: I won't be working on Friday. I've taken a day off.
rows.id: Hari Jumat saya tidak bekerja. Saya sudah ambil cuti.

blocks.text: **The Indonesian trap:** *Besok jam segini saya **sedang** terbang ke Bali* has **sedang** with a future time. Learners drop the -ing and write 'This time tomorrow I will fly to Bali'. Simple *will fly* sounds like the whole trip or a decision you make now. For 'sedang' at a future moment, use **will be + -ing**: *This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.*

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Besok jam segini saya **sedang** terbang ke Bali* punya kata **sedang** dengan waktu masa depan. Pelajar sering membuang -ing dan menulis 'This time tomorrow I will fly to Bali'. *will fly* biasa terdengar seperti seluruh perjalanan atau keputusan yang baru kamu buat. Untuk 'sedang' pada saat tertentu di masa depan, pakai **will be + -ing**: *This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.*

blocks.text: **Two notes.** (1) *Will you be using the car tonight?* is a soft, polite way to ask about someone's plans before you ask for something (it sounds less pushy than *Are you going to use the car?*). Just remember it as a polite phrase. (2) Verbs for **states**, not actions (**know, want, like, believe, need, own**), don't usually take -ing, here or in the present continuous: *Tomorrow you'll know the results*, not 'you'll be knowing'.

id.text: **Dua catatan.** (1) *Will you be using the car tonight?* adalah cara halus dan sopan untuk menanyakan rencana seseorang sebelum kamu meminta sesuatu (terdengar tidak memaksa dibanding *Are you going to use the car?*). Ingat saja sebagai frasa sopan. (2) Kata kerja **keadaan**, bukan kegiatan (**know, want, like, believe, need, own**), biasanya tidak memakai -ing, di sini maupun di present continuous: *Tomorrow you'll know the results*, bukan 'you'll be knowing'.

blocks.prompt: Dimas is flying to Tokyo today. Tokyo is two hours ahead of Jakarta. Complete: Don't phone Dimas at midnight Jakarta time. It'll be 2 am there, so he ___.
blocks.explain: At 2 am he's in the middle of sleeping, so use **will be + -ing**: **he'll be sleeping**. 'will sleep' sounds like he starts sleeping then, and 'will have slept' means the sleep is finished.

id.prompt: Hari ini Dimas terbang ke Tokyo. Waktu Tokyo dua jam lebih cepat dari Jakarta. Lengkapi: Don't phone Dimas at midnight Jakarta time. It'll be 2 am there, so he ___.
id.explain: Jam 2 pagi dia sedang tidur, jadi pakai **will be + -ing**: **he'll be sleeping**. 'will sleep' terdengar seperti dia baru mulai tidur saat itu, dan 'will have slept' berarti tidurnya sudah selesai.

id.title: will be + -ing: sedang di tengah kegiatan

material.title: will have + past participle: done by then

blocks.text:
**will have + past participle** (the **future perfect**) says something will be **finished before** a moment in the future: go forward to that moment, then look back. The **past participle** is the third form you know from the present perfect: *finished, worked, written, left, paid, gone*.
- Positive: *I'll have finished*
- Negative: *I won't have finished*
- Question: *Will you have finished?*

**have** never changes: *She'll have left*, not 'She'll has left'.

The key word is **by** = *paling lambat* (before or at that time): **by Friday, by 2030, by then, by the end of the year**. With a verb, use **by the time** + the **present simple**: *By the time you get here, …* (= saat kamu sampai nanti, … sudah …).

id.text:
**will have + past participle** (**future perfect**) mengatakan sesuatu akan **sudah selesai sebelum** saat tertentu di masa depan: bayangkan kamu maju ke saat itu, lalu menoleh ke belakang. **Past participle** adalah bentuk ketiga yang kamu kenal dari present perfect: *finished, worked, written, left, paid, gone*.
- Positif: *I'll have finished*
- Negatif: *I won't have finished*
- Pertanyaan: *Will you have finished?*

**have** tidak pernah berubah: *She'll have left*, bukan 'She'll has left'.

Kata kuncinya **by** = *paling lambat* (sebelum atau tepat pada waktu itu): **by Friday, by 2030, by then, by the end of the year**. Dengan kata kerja, pakai **by the time** + **present simple**: *By the time you get here, …* (= saat kamu sampai nanti, … sudah …).

rows.en: By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.
rows.id: Paling lambat tahun 2030 kuliah saya sudah selesai.

rows.en: The film starts at 7. By the time we get there, it'll have started.
rows.id: Filmnya mulai jam 7. Saat kita sampai nanti, filmnya sudah mulai.
rows.note: by the time + present (get), then will have

id.note: by the time + present (get), lalu will have

rows.en: Don't worry, I'll have sent the invoice by Friday.
rows.id: Tenang, paling lambat Jumat tagihannya sudah saya kirim.

rows.en: She won't have finished her shift by 9.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *Tahun 2030 saya **sudah** lulus* has **sudah** with a future time. Learners write 'By 2030 I already graduate' or 'I have finished by 2030'. The present perfect (*have finished*) is for **up to now**; for 'already done at a future moment', add **will**: *By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.*

**by or until?** **by** = paling lambat, a deadline: *I'll have finished it by Friday*. **until** = sampai, the action goes on the whole time: *I'll be at the office until 6*.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Tahun 2030 saya **sudah** lulus* punya kata **sudah** dengan waktu masa depan. Pelajar menulis 'By 2030 I already graduate' atau 'I have finished by 2030'. Present perfect (*have finished*) untuk **sampai sekarang**; untuk 'sudah selesai pada saat tertentu di masa depan', tambahkan **will**: *By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.*

**by atau until?** **by** = paling lambat, sebuah tenggat: *I'll have finished it by Friday*. **until** = sampai, kegiatannya berlangsung terus selama itu: *I'll be at the office until 6*.

blocks.text:
**Is 'I'll finish the report by Friday' wrong?** No: as a plan or a promise it's fine. The future perfect adds the picture 'at that moment, it's already done', and you need it when you describe the situation at that moment, especially with **by the time** or **already**: *By the time you wake up, I'll already have left.* ('By the time you wake up, I'll leave' is wrong.)

In speech, *have* is weak: *I'll have left* sounds like 'I'll-ev left'. Never write 'I'll of left'.

id.text:
**Apakah 'I'll finish the report by Friday' salah?** Tidak: sebagai rencana atau janji, kalimat itu benar. Future perfect menambahkan gambaran 'pada saat itu, sudah selesai', dan kamu memerlukannya saat menggambarkan keadaan pada saat itu, terutama dengan **by the time** atau **already**: *By the time you wake up, I'll already have left.* ('By the time you wake up, I'll leave' salah.)

Saat bicara, *have* diucapkan lemah: *I'll have left* terdengar seperti 'ail-ev left'. Jangan pernah menulis 'I'll of left'.

blocks.prompt: Your manager needs the slides for a meeting on Friday afternoon. You: 'I'll have finished the slides ___ Friday morning.'
blocks.explain: A deadline (paling lambat) → **by Friday morning**. 'until' means the action goes on the whole time up to then, and 'since' is for a starting point in the past.

id.prompt: Manajermu butuh slide untuk rapat hari Jumat sore. Kamu: 'I'll have finished the slides ___ Friday morning.'
id.explain: Ini tenggat (paling lambat) → **by Friday morning**. 'until' berarti kegiatannya berlangsung terus sampai saat itu, dan 'since' untuk titik mulai di masa lalu.

id.title: will have + past participle: sudah selesai saat itu

material.title: will have been + -ing: how long, up to then

blocks.text:
**will have been + -ing** (the **future perfect continuous**) looks at a **duration** (how long) up to a moment in the future. It's the present perfect continuous you know (*I've been working here for four years*) moved into the future. You usually need two things: **for + a period**, and **the moment** (*by June, next year, when …, by the time …*).

*I started here in June 2022. By June 2027, I'll have been working here for five years.*

The form is the same for every subject: *I'll have been waiting*, *She'll have been teaching*, *They'll have been travelling*.

id.text:
**will have been + -ing** (**future perfect continuous**) melihat **lamanya** sebuah kegiatan sampai saat tertentu di masa depan. Ini present perfect continuous yang sudah kamu kenal (*I've been working here for four years*) yang dipindah ke masa depan. Biasanya kamu perlu dua hal: **for + lamanya**, dan **saatnya** (*by June, next year, when …, by the time …*).

*I started here in June 2022. By June 2027, I'll have been working here for five years.*

Bentuknya sama untuk semua subjek: *I'll have been waiting*, *She'll have been teaching*, *They'll have been travelling*.

rows.en: By June I'll have been working here for five years.
rows.id: Juni nanti, sudah lima tahun saya bekerja di sini.

rows.en: By the time the plane lands, we'll have been travelling for 20 hours.
rows.id: Saat pesawatnya mendarat nanti, kami sudah 20 jam dalam perjalanan.

id.note: bahasa Inggris British: travelling, Amerika: traveling

rows.en: Next month Rina will have been learning English for three years.
rows.id: Bulan depan sudah tiga tahun Rina belajar bahasa Inggris.

rows.en: By 9 pm the team will have been working on the app for twelve hours.
rows.id: Jam 9 malam nanti, tim itu sudah dua belas jam mengerjakan aplikasinya.

blocks.text: **The Indonesian trap:** *Juni nanti **sudah** lima tahun saya kerja di sini* → learners say 'In June I work here five years' or 'In June I have worked here five years'. English needs the future (**will**), the duration form (**have been + -ing**) and **for**: *By June I'll have been working here for five years.*

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Juni nanti **sudah** lima tahun saya kerja di sini* → pelajar bilang 'In June I work here five years' atau 'In June I have worked here five years'. Bahasa Inggris perlu bentuk masa depan (**will**), bentuk lamanya (**have been + -ing**) dan **for**: *By June I'll have been working here for five years.*

blocks.text: **A tendency, not a hard rule:** with **live, work, study, teach**, the future perfect simple is also correct: *By June I'll have worked here for five years*. The continuous version puts more focus on the activity going on. With **state verbs** (**know, be**, **have** for owning), use only the simple: *By May I'll have known Sari for ten years*, not 'have been knowing'.

id.text: **Kecenderungan, bukan aturan mutlak:** dengan **live, work, study, teach**, future perfect simple juga benar: *By June I'll have worked here for five years*. Bentuk continuous lebih menonjolkan kegiatan yang terus berjalan. Dengan **kata kerja keadaan** (**know, be**, **have** untuk memiliki), pakai bentuk simple saja: *By May I'll have known Sari for ten years*, bukan 'have been knowing'.

blocks.prompt: Budi and Sari started going out in March 2017. Complete: In March 2027, they ___ together for ten years.
blocks.explain: How long, up to a future moment (March 2027) → **will have been + -ing**: **they'll have been going out together for ten years**. 'will be going out' only says it's happening then, without the duration, and 'have been going out' is up to now, not up to 2027.

id.prompt: Budi dan Sari mulai pacaran (going out) pada bulan Maret 2017. Lengkapi: In March 2027, they ___ together for ten years.
id.explain: Lamanya sampai saat tertentu di masa depan (Maret 2027) → **will have been + -ing**: **they'll have been going out together for ten years**. 'will be going out' hanya mengatakan sedang terjadi saat itu, tanpa lamanya, dan 'have been going out' berarti sampai sekarang, bukan sampai 2027.

id.title: will have been + -ing: sudah berapa lama saat itu

material.title: Choosing, and no will after when

blocks.text:
To choose, picture the moment in the future and ask:
- **What's happening at that moment?** (in the middle) → **will be + -ing**
- **What's already done by then?** → **will have + past participle**
- **How long will it have been going on by then?** (for + a period) → **will have been + -ing**

The time-clause rule from the B1 lesson still works: after **when, after, before, as soon as, until** and **by the time**, there's **no will**, not even in these new forms. Use the **present simple**, or the **present perfect** to stress 'finished': *Call me when you've finished* (or *when you finish*), not 'when you will have finished'. A question is different: *When will you have finished?* is correct.

id.text:
Untuk memilih, bayangkan saat tertentu di masa depan dan tanyakan:
- **Apa yang sedang terjadi saat itu?** (di tengah kegiatan) → **will be + -ing**
- **Apa yang sudah selesai saat itu?** → **will have + past participle**
- **Sudah berapa lama kegiatannya berjalan saat itu?** (for + lamanya) → **will have been + -ing**

Aturan time clause dari pelajaran B1 tetap berlaku: setelah **when, after, before, as soon as, until** dan **by the time**, **tidak ada will**, termasuk di bentuk-bentuk baru ini. Pakai **present simple**, atau **present perfect** untuk menekankan 'sudah selesai': *Call me when you've finished* (atau *when you finish*), bukan 'when you will have finished'. Pertanyaan berbeda: *When will you have finished?* benar.

id.note: time clause: present perfect, tanpa will

blocks.text: **The Indonesian trap:** *Kabari saya kalau **sudah** selesai* has **sudah** and is about the future, so learners write 'Tell me when you will have finished'. In the time clause, English says **when you've finished** (or **when you finish**). The **will** goes in the other part: *I'll call you when I've finished.*

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Kabari saya kalau **sudah** selesai* punya kata **sudah** dan membicarakan masa depan, jadi pelajar menulis 'Tell me when you will have finished'. Di time clause, bahasa Inggris bilang **when you've finished** (atau **when you finish**). **will** ditaruh di bagian yang lain: *I'll call you when I've finished.*

blocks.prompt: Rina wants to borrow your novel. You: 'Sure. I'll lend it to you after I ___ it.'
blocks.explain: After **after** (a time clause), there's no will: use the present perfect, **after I've read it** (*after I read it* is also fine). 'will have read' and 'will be reading' put will in the time clause.

id.prompt: Rina mau meminjam novelmu. Kamu: 'Sure. I'll lend it to you after I ___ it.'
id.explain: Setelah **after** (time clause), tidak ada will: pakai present perfect, **after I've read it** (*after I read it* juga benar). 'will have read' dan 'will be reading' menaruh will di time clause.

resources.title: Future continuous and future perfect
resources.note: Will be + -ing and will have + past participle explained with time phrases like by and by the time, plus two short gap-fill tests. B1–B2 level. It doesn't cover the future perfect continuous (will have been + -ing).

id.note: Penjelasan will be + -ing dan will have + past participle dengan frasa waktu seperti by dan by the time, plus dua tes isian singkat. Level B1–B2. Halaman ini tidak membahas future perfect continuous (will have been + -ing).

id.intro: Kamu sudah memakai will, going to dan present continuous untuk masa depan. Sekarang kamu berdiri di satu saat di masa depan dan menggambarkannya dengan tiga cara: apa yang sedang kamu lakukan saat itu (This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali), apa yang sudah selesai saat itu (By 2030 I'll have finished my degree), dan sudah berapa lama kamu melakukannya (By June I'll have been working here for five years). Pemanasan: besok jam 9 pagi kamu sedang apa?
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya 'At 8 I'll call you' dan 'At 8 I'll be driving'?
Apakah 'I'll finish it by Friday' salah?
Kapan pakai 'will have worked' dan kapan 'will have been working'?

assessment.fpc-1: Temukan kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: This time next week I will lie on a beach in Lombok.
assessment.fpc-2: Lengkapi dengan will dan kata kerja dalam kurung. Ujian SIM Budi besok jam 2 sampai jam 3 siang. Dia bilang ke ibunya: 'Don't call me at 2:30. I ___ (take) my driving test then.'
assessment.fpc-3: Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung. Pukul 23.45 Budi masih di kantornya di Jalan Sudirman. Dia berpikir: 'By the time I get to Manggarai station, the last KRL ___ (leave). I'll have to take an ojek.'
assessment.fpc-4: Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung. Sari akan membayar cicilan terakhir motornya bulan Maret. Dia bilang: 'By April, I ___ (pay) for it completely. No more instalments!'
assessment.fpc-5: Temukan kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: Text me when you will have arrived at the hotel.
assessment.fpc-6: Lengkapi dengan future perfect continuous dari kata kerja dalam kurung. Pak Hasan membuka warungnya di Surabaya pada bulan Desember 2016. Dia bilang: 'By this December, I ___ (run) it for ten years!'
assessment.fpc-7: Lengkapi dengan future perfect continuous dari kata kerja wait. Rina mulai menunggu bus TransJakarta jam 7.00. Sekarang jam 7.40, dan menurut aplikasinya bus akan datang jam 8.00. Rina: 'When the bus comes, I ___ for an hour!'
